result.title: Gradient Descent on Two ReLU Neurons: Global Landscape and Bifurcation Dynamics
result.summary: Understanding how gradient descent learns features remains a central challenge in neural network theory. We study this question in a minimal multi-index setting that already exhibits rich multi-phase gradient dynamics: a well-specified two-neuron ReLU teacher-student model under isotropic Gaussian inputs, trained by population gradient flow from small initialization. We show that the dynamics are organized by two directions: the "easy" bisector direction, which carries the leading signal, and the "hard" splitting direction, which governs specialization. To characterize the loss structure and learning behavior, we analyze the population squared-loss landscape and show that every critical point with both student weights nonzero is either a global minimum or a saddle. We then track the gradient-flow trajectory, showing that student neurons first collapse toward a bisector saddle before escaping and specializing to teacher neurons. Our results provide both a landscape and dynamics account of the multi-phase symmetry-breaking behavior that arises in a simple multi-index model and under standard algorithmic and architectural choices.

AI.brief_summary: 论文在双神经元 ReLU teacher-student 模型（各向同性高斯输入、小初始化、population gradient flow）下分析平方损失景观与梯度流轨迹，证明两权重均非零的临界点只能是全局最优或鞍点，并刻画学生神经元先向角平分线鞍点坍缩、随后逃逸并各自专门化的多阶段对称破缺过程。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「先坍缩至鞍点、再分化解耦」的多阶段对称破缺与鞍点逃逸分析，可能为理解多条 latent 推理轨迹或潜在状态槽在训练中如何形成分工、初始化与宽度如何影响专门化提供概念与诊断线索；但该工作纯属优化理论、无视觉或多模态成分，迁移需较多核查。
